newsitem.title: USA: Levitt to announce backers of lwyr pay-to-play ban.
newsitem.headline: Levitt to announce backers of lwyr pay-to-play ban.

text.p: The number of prominent attorneys nationwide that back SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt's push for a ban on pay-to-play by muni lawyers is growing leaps and bounds, the chairman will tell a press briefing Wednesday, according to an aide.
The numbers have "increased considerably," Chris Ullman, director of public affairs for the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a telephone interview.
Levitt recently announced the formation of a prestigious Lawyers Committee to End Pay-to-Play headed by Judge William Webster.

Ullman said Levitt at 1415 EDT on Wednesday will announce names of the rapidly expanding list of lawyers that have joined the committee in signing a resolution calling for a ban on pay-to-play by lawyers.
Over 30 lawyers had signed the resolution by July 3 and the list is growing fast, Ullman said.
Wednesday's press conference comes less than a week before American Bar Association delegates meeting in San Francisco are scheduled to vote on a pay-to-play resolution.
The draft ABA policy would condemn pay-to-play among lawyers and calls for a task force to study whether a ban is appropriate.
Levitt wants bond lawyers to follow the lead of the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, which last year called for a bank on lawyers' pay-to-play.
"They thought we were out in left field" when the chairman first started pushing a lawyers' ban, Ullman said. "We feel we are making great progress."
Pay-to-play refers to muni bond professionals who give contributions to elected state and local officials in return for bond business, or even to put placed in the running for such business.
